analysis.title: GS EUROPEAN EXPRESS: Data Centers | Rheinmetall | Argenx | Naturgy | Pluxee Upgrade | Macro | Global | Corporate Access
key_insights: Europe datacenter build-out is unaffected by the US midterm outcome per a call with the EUDCA Secretary General. GS describes the European DC market as in a super-cycle.
On a prudent forecast, the European DC market could more than double by the early 2030s.
Power infrastructure, power grids in particular, is the single largest bottleneck for European datacenters, which implies ongoing tailwinds for the power industry.

Power generators with land, grid connection points and the ability to sign energy supply contracts should benefit most. GS flags Solaria (Buy, on CL), Drax (Buy), RWE (Buy, on CL), PPC (Buy) and Fortum (Neutral).
European power grids are likely to see accelerating capex (EON Buy named). Equipment makers are a key way to gain exposure: Siemens Energy (Buy, on CL), Vestas and Nordex.

Rheinmetall CEO fireside chat: management is confident the Arminius vehicle programme will proceed. Quantities and specifications are largely agreed and pricing is the main open issue. Signing in early 2027 is seen as achievable, but management will not commit to a precise timetable.

Argenx announced the acquisition of Unnatural Products (oral macrocyclic peptides) for up to $1.15bn: $550mn upfront plus $595mn in development and regulatory milestones. Closing is expected by year-end. FY26 expense guidance is unchanged and FY27 guidance is due January 2027.

Naturgy: strict return and valuation criteria could limit external growth in grids and renewables. GS sees buying depressed-valuation renewable platforms as an attractive growth route and simulates acquisitions of renewable developers and retail customers as a positive. Buy, 19% upside. Enagas stays Sell on structural headwinds.

Pluxee upgraded to Neutral from Sell after the shares fell 31% since the 14 Oct 2024 Sell List addition, underperforming by 55pp on regulatory headwinds, mainly in Brazil. Management guided FY27 EBITDA to at least €440mn, implying a yoy decline of up to 10%, well below lowered expectations, due to equalization of merchant terms in Brazil after the PAT reform. GS cuts EPS estimates by c.10%.

GOAL Kickstart: after Democrats won the midterms with a larger-than-expected majority in the House and Senate, markets are focused on political and regulatory uncertainty around energy and the AI/data center buildout. Brent fell over 16% and US equities sold off sharply, with one of the largest spikes in Nasdaq volatility since March 2020.

GS Risk Appetite Indicator fell to -0.6 and positioning is lighter. GS remains overweight equities over 3m and 12m on earnings support, lighter positioning and lower valuations, and overweight cash and bonds.

Global Rates Notes: GS expects reserve management purchases to resume this month at $10bn/month, settling around $25bn/month from 2Q27, keeping reserves stable at around 11% of bank assets. Treasury supply-demand and debt-limit swings point to a bumpier path and more repo rate volatility.

Other notable items: Nvidia 3Q preview expects strong results and guidance with focus on power/shell and customer funding needs through 2028. Constellation Energy (CEG) 3Q EPS beat GS and consensus with 2026 guidance raised. Daikin upgraded to Buy from Neutral. Semiconductors note on value after the sector-wide pullback.
Europe PT changes: Interparfums raised to €36.75 from €32.00 (+14.8%, Buy). Europe EPS change: Verisure cut to €0.47 from €0.57 (-16.4%, Buy).
